title: Mindfulness of breathing: the first four steps
framing: guided, explanatory, no scores or win states
intro: The Ānāpānasati Sutta (Majjhima Nikāya 118) describes mindfulness of breathing in sixteen steps, grouped in four sets of four. This walkthrough follows the first set, as the text lays it out. It explains a practice; you may follow along or simply read. Nothing is scored.

sources.cite: Ānāpānasati Sutta: Mindfulness of Breathing (MN 118, PTS M iii 78), translated from the Pali by Thanissaro Bhikkhu. Access to Insight.

steps.text: The sutta sets the scene: a monk goes to a quiet place (the wilderness, the shade of a tree, an empty building), sits with legs crossed and body upright, and sets mindfulness to the fore.
steps.pacing_note: Display choice; the text gives no timing.

steps.text: Step one: breathing in long, he knows he is breathing in long; breathing out long, he knows he is breathing out long.
steps.pacing_note: Display choice (one slow breath cycle); the text gives no timing.

steps.text: Step two: breathing in short, he knows he is breathing in short; breathing out short, he knows he is breathing out short.
steps.pacing_note: Display choice; the text gives no timing.

steps.text: Step three: he trains himself to breathe in and out sensitive to the entire body.
steps.pacing_note: Display choice; the text gives no timing.

steps.text: Step four: he trains himself to breathe in and out calming the bodily processes. The sutta goes on to twelve more steps, on feeling, mind and mental qualities; the archive's Buddhism chapter places this practice within the path's training in meditation.
steps.pacing_note: Display choice; the text gives no timing.
